---
title: "Before the day"
aliases:
  - /tracks/one-day-replication/before.html
---
The day runs in the browser lab, so the one thing to do beforehand is to open the lab once on the machine you will use and let it load. Reading the case study is the best preparation for the rest; installing R and an IDE is optional.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) | Open it on the machine and in the browser that you will use, wait for the R engine to load (10 to 30 seconds on a slow connection), and run the cell of Task 1. If it reports 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, you are set. | 5 minutes |
| [Case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd) | The original study, its questions, data and selections; SCORE and the Multi100 project; the five reanalyses and an assessment of their choices; and how Multi100 put their results on one scale. Every part of the day works on this case. | 60 minutes |
| [Exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) | The claim you will be working on, and the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found when they reanalysed it. | 10 minutes |
| [Setup](../../setup.qmd) | Optional. Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the workspace and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure. The [help page](../../help.qmd) has the problems that other participants have met. | 30 to 60 minutes, once |
| [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) | Optional. Archives, the OSF and the preregistration templates, in more depth than the day has time for. | 30 minutes |

**By the start of the day** the browser lab loads on your machine, and you know what the claim is and how far apart the results of the five Multi100 analysts are.
